'''Kuno Ruben Gabriel''' (1929–2003) was a [[statistician]] known for the inventing the [[biplot]]<ref name="rochester-obit"/> and the [[Gabriel graph]]<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Aurenhammer | first1 = Franz |author1-link=Franz Aurenhammer
 | last2 = Klein | first2 = Rolf
 | contribution = Voronoi diagrams
 | doi = 10.1016/B978-044482537-7/50006-1
 | mr = 1746678
 | pages = 201–290
 | publisher = North-Holland, Amsterdam
 | title = Handbook of computational geometry
 | year = 2000}}. See in particular [https://books.google.com/books?id=uZdAqAWB3BcC&pg=PA273 pp. 273–274].</ref> and for his work in statistical [[meteorology]].<ref name="rochester-obit">[http://www.rochester.edu/news/show.php?id=1450 Kuno Ruben Gabriel, Pioneer of Statistics, Dies], University of Rochester, May 30, 2003, retrieved 2014-07-02.</ref>

Gabriel was born in [[Germany]], emigrated to [[France]], grew up in [[Israel]], was educated at the [[London School of Economics]] and the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], taught at the Hebrew University until 1975, and then moved to the [[University of Rochester]] where he remained until his retirement in 1997. He died on May 25, 2003.<ref name="rochester-obit"/><ref name="jsfs">{{citation|title=Nécrologie. Kuno Ruben Gabriel (1929–2003)|journal=Journal de la Société Française de Statistique|volume=143|issue=3–4|year=2002|page=3|url=http://www.numdam.org/item?id=JSFS_2002__143_3-4_3_0|first=Henri|last=Caussinus|language=French}}.</ref>

He was a [[fellow]] of the [[American Statistical Association]] and the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], and was an elected member of the [[International Statistical Institute]].<ref name="rochester-obit"/>
